252 253 const executor = await createFraIAgentExecutor({ 254 model: "gpt-4o-mini", 255 verbose: true 256 }); 257 258 const result = await executor.invoke({ 259 input: "scan the repository", 260 chat_history: [] 261 }); 262 263 console.log(result.output); 264 ``` 265 266 `frai-agent` reuses FRAI's configuration system, so it automatically discovers your `OPENAI_API_KEY` from `.env` or global config. 267 268 --- 269 270 ## Responsible AI Gate (`frai gate`) 271 272 **The idea in one sentence: an AI feature spec is not done until seven responsible-AI questions are answered, and the gate blocks the build until they are.** 273 274 275 276 The seven checks: **risk tier** (EU AI Act-aligned; high-risk needs a named human sign-off) · **data & privacy** · **human oversight** · **evaluation thresholds** · **bias & fairness** · **monitoring & rollback** · **transparency & incidents**. Verdicts: ✅ PASS · ⚠️ WARN · ⛔ BLOCK (exit 1). 277 278 ### Add it to any app in 60 seconds 279 280 Works in any repo - new app, existing app, any language: 281 282 ```bash 283 npx frai-gate init --ci 284 ``` 285 286 That drops `FRAI-SPEC.md` (a spec template with the gate built in) and a GitHub Action that runs the gate on every PR. Answer the gate, then: 287 288 ```bash 289 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md 290 ``` 291 292 No API key needed for the check. Two smarter commands use a read-only agent (Claude Code auth or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`): 293 294 ```bash 295 npx frai-gate draft # scans YOUR code and drafts the gate answers from it, 296 # with file:line citations and NEEDS HUMAN INPUT markers 297 npx frai-gate check FRAI-SPEC.md --smart # adversarial review: catches vague answers and 298 # spec claims your code contradicts 299 ``` 300 301 ### If you build with AI coding agents 302 303 ```bash 304 npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills 305 ``` 306 307 installs the `responsible-ai-spec` skill: every spec your agent writes includes the gate, and the agent is forbidden from self-approving high-risk features - a named human signs. Claude Code users in this repo also get `/rai-spec`. 308 309 Everything is also available as `frai gate ...` inside the main CLI, and programmatically via `import { validateSpec } from 'frai-gate'`. Worked example (the one from the demo video): [`examples/support-triage-demo/`](examples/support-triage-demo). Design notes: `docs/rai-gate-design.md`. 310 311 --- 312 313 ## Local Development 314 315 Clone the repository and work from source: 316 ```bash 317 pnpm install 318 pnpm --filter frai run build 319 node packages/frai-cli/dist/index.js --help 320 ``` 321 322 During development you can install the CLI locally without publishing: 323 ```bash 324 pnpm install --global ./packages/frai-cli 325 # then 326 frai --setup 327 ``` 328 329 Store your OpenAI key by running the CLI setup flow or setting `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `.env`. 330 331 --- 332 333 ## Publishing (Maintainers) 334 335 FRAI ships as two npm packages and they must be published independently. 336 337 1. Bump versions in `packages/frai-core/package.json` and `packages/frai-cli/package.json`. Update the CLI dependency to match the published `frai-core` version (drop `workspace:*`). 338 2. Build the CLI: 339 ```bash 340 pnpm --filter frai run build 341 ``` 342 3. Publish `frai-core` first, then `frai`: 343 ```bash 344 cd packages/frai-core && npm publish 345 cd ../frai-cli && npm publish 346 ``` 347 4. Verify on npm: 348 ```bash 349 npm view frai versions --json 350 npm view frai-core versions --json 351 ``` 352 353 --- 354 355 ## Learn More 356 - Website: [frai.cc](https://frai.cc) 357 - NPM package: [frai](https://www.npmjs.com/package/frai) 358 - docs/ai_feature_backlog.md – roadmap for AI capabilities. 359 - docs/eval_harness_design.md – evaluation harness design notes. 360 - docs/architecture-target.md – monorepo architecture. 361 362 *Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence* 363

17 18 # FRAI · Framework of Responsible Artificial Intelligence 19 20 ![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/frai) 21 ![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dt/frai) 22 23 **Live platform:** [frai.cc](https://www.frai.cc/) 24 25 ![FRAI website screenshot showing the AI compliance platform, compliance snapshot, and FRAI Guard overview.](assets/frai_cc_screenshot.png) 26 27 FRAI is an open-source toolkit that helps teams launch AI features responsibly. It guides you through evidence gathering, scans your code, and assembles documentation you can hand to reviewers: implementation checklists, model cards, risk files, evaluation reports, and compliance-aware RAG indexes. The toolkit ships as four packages that work together: 28 29 - `frai` – the command-line app with ready-to-run workflows. 30 - `frai-core` – the reusable SDK that powers the CLI and any custom integrations. 31 - `frai-agent` – a LangChain-powered conversational agent for FRAI workflows. 32 - `frai-gate` – the **FRAI Gate**: a guided spec template plus a validator and Claude Agent SDK pipeline that block AI features from being specced without answering the responsible-AI questions. (The matching agent skill lives in [frai-skills](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills).) 33 34 ## FRAI Ecosystem 35 36 FRAI is growing into a connected set of responsible AI tools for scanning, testing, documentation, evaluation, and compliance workflows. 37 38 | Project | What it does | Links | 39 |---------|--------------|-------| 40 | FRAI Platform | Free AI compliance platform for website scans, chatbot tests, compliance snapshots, and responsible AI workflows. | [Website](https://www.frai.cc/) | 41 | FRAI CLI / SDK | Open-source CLI and reusable SDK for responsible AI docs, code scanning, RAG indexing, evaluations, and governance workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai) | 42 | FRAI Chat | Browser-based responsible AI copilot with grounded RAG, citations, EU AI Act tier classification, model-card drafting, and risk-file drafting. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-chat) · [Live demo](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-chat/) | 43 | FRAI Benchmark | Open-source safety and compliance benchmark with a model registry, test suites, automated runs, and an interactive leaderboard. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-benchmark) · [Leaderboard](https://sebuzdugan.github.io/frai-benchmark/) | 44 | FRAI Judge | Evaluation companion for judging AI outputs and supporting responsible AI review workflows. | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-judge) | 45 | FRAI Skills | Agent skills for responsible AI engineering - the FRAI Gate spec workflow for AI coding agents (`npx skills add sebuzdugan/frai-skills`). | [GitHub](https://github.com/sebuzdugan/frai-skills) | 46 47 ### Short Answer 48 - `frai-core` is the library/SDK. Use it when you are embedding FRAI capabilities into your own tools, servers, automations, or extensions. 49 - `frai` is the CLI. It wraps `frai-core` to deliver an end-user experience with no coding required. 50 51 ### Why Keep Both? 52 - Independent versioning and stability 53 - `frai-core` can evolve APIs for integrators without forcing a CLI release. 54 - `frai` can improve UX/commands without breaking programmatic users. 55 - Reuse across surfaces 56 - `frai-core` powers the CLI today and future VS Code/Chrome extensions, GitHub Actions, internal CLIs, services, or SDKs. 57 - Smaller, focused installs 58 - Operators install the CLI. 59 - Builders install only the core library they need. 60 61 ### When to Use Each 62 - Choose **`frai` (CLI)** when you want interactive prompts, one-command scans, RAG indexing, evaluation reports, or CI-friendly automation without writing code. 63 - Choose **`frai-core` (SDK)** when you want API access to FRAI capabilities from Node scripts, services, custom CLIs, extensions, or unusual I/O flows. 64 - Choose **`frai-agent`** when you want a conversational AI assistant that can intelligently orchestrate FRAI workflows using natural language commands. 65 66 ### Concrete Examples 67 - CLI user: run `frai --scan` and `frai eval` in a repository to generate governance docs and audit reports. 68 - Library user: call `Documents.generateDocuments` from an internal portal to produce standardized docs, use `Scanners.scanCodebase` inside a GitHub Action, or embed `Rag.indexDocuments` inside a VS Code extension for grounded hints. 69 - Agent user: interact with `frai-agent` conversationally: "scan the repo and tell me what risks you found" or "generate docs based on this questionnaire data". 70 71 In short: CLI = product; Core = platform. They overlap in capability on purpose but target different audiences and distribution needs. 72 73 --- 74 75 ## Getting Started with the CLI 76 77 1. Install the published CLI: 78 ```bash 79 npm install -g frai 80 ``` 81 2. Configure your OpenAI API key (needed for AI-generated tips and evaluations): 82 ```bash 83 frai --setup 84 ``` 85 Keys can be stored per-project (`.env`) or globally (`~/.config/frai/config`). You can also provide a one-off key using `frai --key sk-...`. 86 3. Run the interactive workflow: 87 ```bash 88 frai 89 ``` 90 FRAI walks you through feature discovery, writes `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`, and optionally exports PDFs. 91 92 Generated artefacts live in your current working directory. Supplementary commands cover scanning, evaluation, RAG indexing, and fine-tuning governance. 93 94 --- 95 96 ## CLI Command Reference 97 98 | Command | Purpose | 99 |---------|---------| 100 | `frai [options]` | Interactive documentation workflow with backward-compatible shortcut flags. | 101 | `frai generate [options]` | Explicit interactive workflow command. | 102 | `frai scan [--ci] [--json]` | Scan the repository for AI/ML indicators. | 103 | `frai setup [--key ] [--global]` | Store an OpenAI API key locally or globally. | 104 | `frai config` | Show key configuration status. | 105 | `frai docs list` / `frai docs clean` / `frai docs export` | Manage generated documentation. | 106 | `frai rag index [options]` | Build a local compliance-aware vector index. | 107 | `frai eval --outputs [...]` | Run baseline evaluation metrics and write reports. | 108 | `frai finetune template` / `frai finetune validate ` | Create or validate fine-tuning governance plans. | 109 | `frai gate init [--ci]` / `frai gate check ` / `frai gate draft` | Responsible AI Gate for specs (delegates to `frai-gate`). | 110 | `frai update` | Check npm for the latest CLI release. | 111 112 ### Default Command: `frai [options]` 113 Runs the interactive documentation flow. Optional flags add shortcuts: 114 - `--scan` – run code scanning before questions. 115 - `--ci` – exit after scanning when no AI indicators are detected. 116 - `--setup` – jump directly into key configuration. 117 - `--key ` / `--global` – provide a key and optionally persist it globally. 118 - `--list-docs` / `--clean` – list or remove generated docs. 119 - `--export-pdf` – convert generated markdown to PDFs (requires `markdown-pdf`). 120 - `--show-config` – display key storage status. 121 - `--update` – check npm for a newer CLI version. 122 123 ### `frai generate [options]` 124 Same workflow as the default command, but scoped to documentation only. Options mirror the defaults: `--scan`, `--ci`, `--key`, `--global`, `--export-pdf`, and `--show-config`. 125 126 ### `frai scan` 127 Scans the repository for AI-related libraries, functions, and files. Use `--ci` for non-interactive mode or `--json` to emit raw JSON. 128 129 ### `frai setup` 130 Guided API key storage. Supply `--key ` for headless use and `--global` to persist at `~/.config/frai/config`. 131 132 ### `frai config` 133 Prints whether local (`.env`) or global configuration holds an API key. 134 135 ### `frai docs` 136 Utilities for generated artefacts: 137 - `frai docs list` – list detected `checklist.md`, `model_card.md`, and `risk_file.md`. 138 - `frai docs clean` – delete generated docs. 139 - `frai docs export` – export docs to PDF via `markdown-pdf`. 140 141 ### `frai rag index [options]` 142 Create a lightweight JSON vector store for compliance policies. 143 - `--input ` – file or directory to index (defaults to cwd). 144 - `--output ` – target JSON file (defaults to `frai-index.json`). 145 - `--chunk-size ` – words per chunk (default 800). 146 - `--extensions ` – allowlisted extensions (default `.md,.markdown,.txt,.json,.yaml,.yml`). 147 148 ### `frai eval` 149 Generate evaluation reports for model outputs. 150 - `--outputs ` *(required)* – JSON file with model outputs. 151 - `--references ` – JSON file with reference answers. 152 - `--report ` – output location (`frai-eval-report.json` by default). 153 - `--format ` – output format (defaults to JSON). Markdown reports include human-readable summaries for review boards. 154 155 ### `frai finetune` 156 Fine-tuning governance helpers: 157 - `frai finetune template [--output ]` – write a governance template JSON (`frai-finetune-plan.json` by default). 158 - `frai finetune validate [--readiness]` – validate a plan and optionally print readiness checkpoints and summaries. 159 160 ### `frai update` 161 Check npm for the latest `frai` release and print upgrade instructions. 162 163 --- 164 165 ## Using `frai-core` (SDK) 166 167 Install from npm: 168 ```bash 169 pnpm add frai-core 170 ``` 171 172 `frai-core` exposes modular helpers that the CLI uses under the hood: 173 - `Questionnaire` – interactive question flows. 174 - `Documents` – generate checklists, model cards, and risk files. 175 - `Scanners` – static analysis for AI indicators. 176 - `Rag` – policy-grounded indexing utilities. 177 - `Eval` – baseline evaluation metrics and report writers. 178 - `Finetune` – governance templates, validation, and readiness scoring. 179 - `Config` & `Providers` – key management and LLM provider wiring. 180 181 Example: generate documentation programmatically. 182 183 ```ts 184 import fs from 'fs/promises'; 185 import inquirer from 'inquirer'; 186 import { Documents, Questionnaire, Scanners } from 'frai-core'; 187 188 const answers = await Questionnaire.runQuestionnaire({ 189 prompt: (questions) => inquirer.prompt(questions) 190 }); 191 192 const { checklist, modelCard, riskFile } = Documents.generateDocuments({ answers }); 193 const scan = Scanners.scanCodebase({ root: process.cwd() }); 194 const aiContext = Documents.buildContextForAITips(answers); 195 196 await fs.writeFile('checklist.md', checklist); 197 await fs.writeFile('model_card.md', modelCard); 198 await fs.writeFile('risk_file.md', riskFile); 199 await fs.writeFile('scan-summary.json', JSON.stringify(scan, null, 2)); 200 await fs.writeFile('ai-context.txt', aiContext);

2	
3	## Goals
4	- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
5	- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
6	- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.
7

9	- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).

11	  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).

15	- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.
16

18	- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.

22	- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.

1	# FRAI Open Source Roadmap
2	
3	## Overview
4	- Mission: deliver a modular, contribution-friendly responsible AI toolkit spanning CLI, SDKs, guardrails, RAG workflows, and evaluation pipelines.
5	- Strategy: refactor the existing `frai` package into a monorepo of reusable modules, layer advanced AI/ML/NLP capabilities, and ship polished developer tooling (CLI, SDKs, VS Code extension, Docker images).
6	- Boundary: keep core compliance workflows open source while allowing optional hand-offs to the commercial FRAI SaaS.
7	
8	## Guiding Engineering Principles
9	- Favour small, composable modules with clear contracts (SOLID, clean architecture).
10	- Maintain full test coverage for new logic; TDD for critical scanners and generators.
11	- Ship with observable metrics and telemetry opt-in to validate user value.
12	- Bias toward DX excellence (typed APIs, docs, examples) to reduce integration friction.
13	- Prioritise AI features that solve concrete governance, audit, and safety pain points for practitioners.
14	
15	## Day-by-Day Plan (First 14 Days)
16	
17	### Week 1 – Restructure & Baseline
18	- ✅ **Day 1:** Run repository inventory, document current architecture, capture CLI behaviour; store findings in `docs/analysis.md`.
19	- ✅ **Day 2:** Finalise target monorepo design, module contracts, and dependency graph; draft `docs/architecture-target.md`.
20	- ✅ **Day 3:** Initialize pnpm/Turborepo workspace, scaffold `packages/frai-core` & `packages/frai-cli`, configure shared lint/test setup.
21	- ✅ **Day 4:** Port configuration & environment handling into `frai-core` modules; create unit tests for config loaders.
22	- ✅ **Day 5:** Migrate questionnaire logic and answer validation into `frai-core`; add Jest/Vitest coverage for prompt flows.
23	- ✅ **Day 6:** Extract document generators/templates, implement override mechanism, and add snapshot tests.
24	- ✅ **Day 7:** Build modular scanning engine with pluggable detectors; run integration tests using `examples/` fixtures.
25	
26	### Week 2 – AI Feature Foundations & Tooling
27	- ✅ **Day 8:** Assemble AI feature backlog with user stories; prioritise RAG, eval, fine-tuning governance; publish roadmap entries.
28	- ✅ **Day 9:** Implement `frai rag index` command, vector store abstraction, and RAG helper modules; cover with CLI tests.
29	- ✅ **Day 10:** Scaffold `frai eval` baseline metrics leveraging open-source models; ensure configurable thresholds and reporting.
30	- ✅ **Day 11:** Implement AI provider abstraction (`frai-core/src/providers`) supporting OpenAI + future adapters with comprehensive test coverage.
31	- ✅ **Day 12:** Draft fine-tuning governance spec (dataset audit, training hooks, bias evals); prototype config schema.
32	- **Day 13:** Develop VS Code MCP endpoint + extension scaffold reading data from `frai-core`; document protocol usage.
33	- **Day 14:** Author problem-solution playbooks (RAG compliance, LLM agent docs) in `/docs`; tie features to user pain points.
34	- **Day 15:** Add opt-in telemetry, gather KPIs (usage of new commands/tests), and produce sprint retrospective summary.
35	
36	## Workstreams (Weeks 3-6)
37	
38	### 1. Clean Architecture & Repo Structure (Weeks 0-2)
39	- Stand up pnpm/Turborepo monorepo with `packages/frai-cli` + `packages/frai-core`; migrate logic from `frai.mjs` into modular `/src` files.
40	- Add ESLint, Prettier, Vitest/Jest, and GitHub Actions for lint + test + coverage enforcement.
41	- Expose typed interfaces (TypeScript declarations or JSDoc) for generators, scanners, and template APIs.
42	- Publish `v1.2.0-alpha` showcasing the refactor; update README + CHANGELOG accordingly.
43	
44	### 2. AI/ML/NLP Feature Foundations (Weeks 2-4)
45	- Modular scanner engine supporting multi-language detectors and pluggable NLP rule packs.
46	- Launch `frai-rag` helpers for policy/document vectorization and CLI command `frai rag index`.
47	- Implement `frai eval` baseline metrics (bias/toxicity) with extensible hooks; document sample configs.
48	- Design fine-tuning governance toolkit covering dataset audits, training hooks, and post-tuning checks.
49	
50	### 3. Developer Experience & Distribution (Weeks 4-6)
51	- Release `frai-vscode` extension MVP with MCP integration, live checklists, and scan results.
52	- Package Docker images (`frai/cli`, `frai/eval`) and umbrella installers (`npx frai setup`, `pip install frai-suite`).
53	- Publish contributor guidelines, code of conduct, and Phase 1 roadmap issues to invite community participation.

## Exploration Summary: frai-core Package Structure

Based on my thorough exploration of the frai-core package, here's what I found:

### 1. **frai-core Location**
- **Path:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d14/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core`
- **Structure:** ES modules (type: "module")
- **Entry point:** `src/index.js`
- **Main export:** Exports namespace `Eval` from `./eval/index.js`

### 2. **generateReport Function**
**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d14/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` (lines 62-82)

**Current Implementation:**
```javascript
export function generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath,
  referencesPath,
  generatedAt = new Date().toISOString()
})
```

**What it does:**
- Takes an array of evaluations (metric results)
- Creates a metadata object with generatedAt, outputsPath, referencesPath, and totalSamples
- Returns a report object with shape: `{ metadata: {...}, metrics: evaluations }`
- Simply aggregates evaluations into a report structure without any validation

### 3. **runEvaluations Function**
**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d14/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js` (lines 41-60)

**How it works:**
- Takes `outputs`, `references`, and `metrics` (defaults to DEFAULT_METRICS)
- Ensures inputs are arrays using `ensureArray()` helper
- Iterates through metrics array and calls each one:
  - If metric is a function: calls `metric(outs, refs)`
  - If metric has `.evaluate` method: calls `metric.evaluate(outs, refs)`
  - Throws error if metric is invalid
- Returns array of evaluation results

**Current metrics signature:** Each metric returns an object with at minimum:
- `id`: string identifier
- `label`: display name
- `score`: number (0-1 range, or null if unable to compute)
- `total`: number of samples evaluated
- Plus metric-specific fields (matches, flagged, averageDelta, samples, etc.)

### 4. **Metrics Definition & Registry**
**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d14/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js`

**Current Metrics (3 built-in):**

1. **exactMatchMetric** (lines 21-54)
   - Compares outputs vs references for exact text match (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed)
   - Returns: `{ score: (matches/total), matches, samples: [{ index, match, predicted, expected }] }`

2. **toxicityMetric** (lines 56-89)
   - Keyword-based scan for banned terms (default: 'hate', 'kill', 'violence', 'terrorist', 'racist', 'sexist')
   - Returns: `{ score: (safe/total), flagged: count, flaggedSamples: [{ index, terms }] }`

3. **lengthVarianceMetric** (lines 91-127)
   - Measures output vs reference length variance
   - Returns: `{ score: max(0, 1 - avgDelta/500), averageDelta, samples: [{ index, predictedLength, expectedLength, delta }] }`

**Registry Pattern:**
- **No formal registry class.** Instead uses simple array: `export const DEFAULT_METRICS = [exactMatchMetric, toxicityMetric, lengthVarianceMetric]`
- Metrics are functions or objects with `.evaluate` method
- Custom metrics can be passed to `runEvaluations()` via the `metrics` parameter

### 5. **Test Structure**
**Location:** `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d14/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js`

**Testing Framework:** Vitest (vitest: ^1.4.0)

**Test Coverage:**
- `loadDataset()`: Loading outputs and references from JSON files
- `runEvaluations()`: Running default evaluations
- `generateReport()`: Creating reports and writing to disk
- `writeReport()`: Supports both JSON and Markdown formats

**Key test patterns:**
- Uses `fs.mkdtempSync()` for temp test directories
- Cleanup with `afterEach()` hook
- Tests verify metric scores and sample-level details

### 6. **Integration Points**

**CLI Usage** (`frai-cli/src/index.ts`, lines 476-497):
```typescript
function runEvalCommand(options: EvalOptions) {
  const dataset = Eval.loadDataset({...});
  const evaluations = Eval.runEvaluations({...});
  const report = Eval.generateReport({...});
  const resolvedPath = Eval.writeReport({...});
}
```

**CLI Options:**
- `--outputs <file>` (required): path to JSON with model outputs
- `--references <file>` (optional): path to JSON with reference outputs
- `--report <path>`: output report path (defaults: frai-eval-report.json or .md)
- `--format <format>`: 'json' or 'markdown'

### 7. **Current Gaps (No Existing Validation/Thresholds)**

- **No metric thresholds** defined or enforced
- **No validation logic** that checks if metric scores pass/fail
- **No conditional reporting** (e.g., fail if exactMatch < 0.8)
- **No configurable metric parameters** (e.g., custom toxicity term lists passed at evaluation time)
- **No metric weighting** for combined scoring
- **Simple structure** allows easy extension with custom metrics

### 8. **File Organization**
```
packages/frai-core/src/eval/
├── index.js          (main exports: loadDataset, runEvaluations, generateReport, writeReport)
├── index.test.js     (vitest test suite)
├── metrics.js        (metric implementations + DEFAULT_METRICS)
└── reporters.js      (toJson, toMarkdown, resolveReportPath)
```

This structure provides a clean foundation for adding threshold validation features without disrupting existing evaluation flow.

Based on my search of the codebase, here's a comprehensive overview of the metric system:

## 1. What Metrics Exist

There are **three built-in metrics**, defined in `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d14/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js`:

- **`exact_match`** – Case-insensitive string comparison between outputs and references
- **`toxicity`** – Keyword scan for banned/harmful terms (default: 'hate', 'kill', 'violence', 'terrorist', 'racist', 'sexist')
- **`length_variance`** – Measures difference in length between outputs and references; normalized to a 0-1 score

All three are bundled in `DEFAULT_METRICS` export and automatically run unless overridden.

## 2. How Metric Scores Are Stored and Accessed

Each metric returns an object with this structure:
```javascript
{
  id: 'metric_name',           // unique identifier
  label: 'Human Label',        // display name
  score: 0.75,                 // 0-1 value OR null if unavailable
  total: 10,                   // number of samples
  // plus metric-specific fields (matches, flagged, averageDelta, etc.)
}
```

**Accessing scores:**
- In code: directly via `metric.score` property (test at `/private/tmp/100-tricks-runs/d14/without/h2-eval-thresholds/r1/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js:44-48`)
- In reports: wrapped by reporters (`toJson()`, `toMarkdown()`) which display `${metric.score ?? 'n/a'}` when null

Reports are generated via `generateReport()` and stored under `report.metrics[]` array.

## 3. List of Valid Metric IDs

**Current valid IDs:**
- `exact_match`
- `toxicity`
- `length_variance`

These IDs are hardcoded in each metric function and used for filtering evaluations (e.g., `evaluations.find((m) => m.id === 'exact_match')`).

## 4. How Custom Metrics Work

Custom metrics are supported via the `runEvaluations()` function. Pass custom metrics as either:

**Option A – Function signature:**
```javascript
(outputs, references) => ({ id, label, score, ... })
```

**Option B – Object with `evaluate` method:**
```javascript
{ evaluate: (outputs, references) => ({ id, label, score, ... }) }
```

The harness accepts any array of these in the `metrics` parameter to `runEvaluations()`.

## 5. Metrics That Can Have Missing Scores

**All three built-in metrics can return `score: null`** when validation fails:

- **`exact_match`** – Returns `null` when: outputs and references are not both non-empty arrays of equal length. Includes `details` field explaining the error.
- **`toxicity`** – Returns `null` when: no outputs are supplied. Includes `details` field.
- **`length_variance`** – Returns `null` when: outputs and references are not both non-empty arrays of equal length. Includes `details` field.

  label: 'Exact Match',
  score: null,  // <- null when validation fails

  details: 'Outputs and references must be non-empty arrays of equal length...'

  },

# Plan: Add Threshold Validation to `frai eval`

## Context
The `frai eval` command currently always exits with code 0, preventing CI pipelines from gating on evaluation metric scores. This feature adds optional `--threshold` flags to fail the evaluation when metrics fall below specified minimums, enabling quality gates for AI-generated content.

The logic must be implemented in frai-core (not just the CLI) so that SDK users can use `generateReport` with thresholds as well.

## Implementation Overview

### Phase 1: CLI Changes (frai-cli/src/index.ts)

**Location:** Lines 708-717 (eval command definition) and 476-497 (runEvalCommand handler)

1. **Add `--threshold` option to command definition:**
   - Multiple `--threshold` flags allowed (e.g., `--threshold exact_match=0.9 --threshold toxicity=1.0`)
   - Store as array in options object

2. **Parse thresholds in runEvalCommand:**
   - Convert array of strings like `["exact_match=0.9", "toxicity=1.0"]` to object `{ exact_match: 0.9, toxicity: 1.0 }`
   - Validation: Call a frai-core utility to validate the thresholds (see Phase 2)
   - If invalid, call `process.exit(2)` with error message before writing report
   - If valid, pass to `generateReport` as new `thresholds` parameter

### Phase 2: Core Logic (frai-core/src/eval)

**New functions:**

1. **`validateThresholds(thresholds, validMetricIds)`** 
   - Input: `{ metric_id: min_score }` object, array of valid metric IDs
   - Returns: `{ valid: boolean, errors: string[] }`
   - Checks:
     - Each threshold value is a number between 0 and 1
     - Each metric ID exists in validMetricIds
   - Error messages include: which threshold is malformed and list of valid metric IDs

2. **`evaluateThresholds(thresholds, metrics)`**
   - Input: thresholds object, evaluations array from `runEvaluations`
   - Returns: `{ passed: boolean, results: [{ metric, min, score, passed }] }`
   - Logic:
     - For each threshold: look up metric in evaluations by `id`
     - If score is null (missing), set `passed: false`
     - Otherwise: `passed = (score >= min)`
     - Return `passed = true` only if ALL thresholds pass

**Update `generateReport` signature:**
```javascript
export function generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath,
  referencesPath,
  generatedAt = new Date().toISOString(),
  thresholds = null  // NEW: optional { metric_id: min_score } object
})
```

When thresholds provided:
- Call `evaluateThresholds(thresholds, evaluations)`
- Add to report: `report.passed` (boolean) and `report.thresholds` (array of threshold results)

**File: `/packages/frai-core/src/eval/index.js`**
- Add `validateThresholds` export
- Add `evaluateThresholds` export (internal helper)
- Update `generateReport` to accept and process thresholds
- Extract valid metric IDs from the DEFAULT_METRICS constant

### Phase 3: Report Format Updates

**JSON Reports:**
When thresholds are evaluated, add to root level:
```json
{
  "metadata": {...},
  "metrics": [...],
  "passed": true/false,
  "thresholds": [
    { "metric": "exact_match", "min": 0.9, "score": 0.85, "passed": false },
    { "metric": "toxicity", "min": 1.0, "score": 1.0, "passed": true }
  ]
}
```

Without thresholds, report structure unchanged (no `passed` or `thresholds` fields).

**Markdown Reports:**
Add "Thresholds" section if thresholds were evaluated:
```markdown
## Thresholds

| Metric | Minimum | Score | Status |
|--------|---------|-------|--------|
| exact_match | 0.90 | 0.85 | ❌ FAIL |
| toxicity | 1.00 | 1.00 | ✅ PASS |
```

Without thresholds, section omitted (current format unchanged).

**File: `/packages/frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js`**
- Update `toMarkdown()` to conditionally render thresholds section
- Update `toJson()` (already just stringifies, no change needed)

### Phase 4: Exit Code Behavior

**In `runEvalCommand` (frai-cli/src/index.ts):**
1. Parse and validate thresholds → exit 2 if invalid
2. Run evaluation, generate report with thresholds
3. Write report (always)
4. Exit with code based on report:
   - Exit 1 if `report.passed === false`
   - Exit 0 if `report.passed === true` OR `report.passed` field absent (no thresholds)

**Summary:**
- Exit 0: All thresholds pass, or no thresholds specified

# Evaluation Harness Design Notes (Day 10)

## Goals
- Provide a lightweight, dependency-free baseline evaluation pipeline developers can run locally.
- Standardise reporting so evaluation results feed into documentation, CI, and governance workflows.
- Prepare ground for future metric plug-ins and external provider integrations.

## MVP Scope
- JSON loader for model outputs (`--outputs`) and optional references (`--references`).
- Default metrics:
  - Exact match (case-insensitive string comparison).
  - Toxicity keyword scan (simple lexical filter).
  - Length variance (difference between outputs and references).
- Report generation: structured JSON + Markdown summaries.
- CLI command `frai eval` wrapping the core harness.

## Data Expectations
- Outputs/reference files should be JSON arrays. Each element may be a string or object containing `text`/`output` fields.
- Future work: support tabular CSV, scored datasets, multi-turn conversations.

## Extensibility Hooks
- `frai-core/src/eval/metrics.js` exposes `DEFAULT_METRICS`; additional metrics can be registered by passing custom evaluators to `runEvaluations`.
- `writeReport` accepts `format` argument to enable additional exporters (HTML, CSV) later.
- CLI parsing accommodates further evaluation subcommands (e.g., `frai eval bias`).

## Follow-up Tasks
1. Integrate real toxicity/bias models once provider abstraction is implemented (Phase 0 → Providers milestone).
2. Extend datasets loader to support configurable schema mapping.
3. Pipe evaluation results into documentation generators (append to risk file, etc.).

The `frai eval` command supports optional `--threshold` flags to gate CI pipelines on metric scores:

# Threshold Validation Feature Implementation Summary

## Overview
Added `--threshold` option to `frai eval` command to enable CI gating on evaluation metric scores. The feature works for both CLI and SDK users.

## Changes Made

### 1. frai-core/src/eval/index.js
**New Functions:**
- `validateThresholds(thresholds, validMetricIds)` - Validates threshold format and values
  - Checks each threshold value is a number between 0-1
  - Verifies metric IDs exist
  - Returns object with `{ valid: boolean, errors: string[] }`

- `evaluateThresholds(thresholds, metrics)` - Evaluates thresholds against metric scores
  - For each threshold, compares metric score to minimum
  - Treats null scores as failed thresholds
  - Returns `{ passed: boolean, results: Array<{metric, min, score, passed}>}`

**Updated Function:**
- `generateReport()` now accepts optional `thresholds` parameter
  - When thresholds provided, adds `passed` (boolean) and `thresholds` (array) to report
  - Maintains backward compatibility when thresholds not provided

### 2. frai-core/src/eval/reporters.js
**Updated:**
- `toMarkdown()` function now includes "Thresholds" section when thresholds present
  - Renders as markdown table with columns: Metric, Minimum, Score, Status
  - Shows ✅ PASS or ❌ FAIL for each threshold

### 3. frai-cli/src/index.ts
**New Function:**
- `parseThresholds(thresholdStrings)` - Parses CLI threshold arguments
  - Format: `metric_id=value` (e.g., `exact_match=0.9`)
  - Validates format with regex: `^([a-z_]+)=([0-9]*\.?[0-9]+)$`
  - Exits with code 2 for malformed input

**Updated:**
- `EvalOptions` interface adds optional `threshold?: string[]` field
- `runEvalCommand()` function:
  - Parses threshold strings
  - Validates against actual metric IDs from evaluations
  - Passes thresholds to `generateReport()`
  - Exits with code 1 if any threshold fails, 0 otherwise

- CLI command definition adds `--threshold <metric=value>` option (repeatable)

### 4. frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js
**New Tests:**
- `validateThresholds` with valid/invalid values
- `evaluateThresholds` with passing/failing metrics
- Threshold failures with null scores
- Report generation with/without thresholds
- Markdown report formatting with thresholds table

### 5. docs/eval_harness_design.md
**Added:**
- "Threshold Validation" section documenting:
  - Command syntax and usage
  - Valid metric IDs
  - Threshold format requirements
  - Exit codes and meanings
  - SDK usage example

## Behavior

### Without `--threshold`
- Report structure unchanged (no `passed` or `thresholds` fields)
- Exit code always 0 (unless error occurs)
- Fully backward compatible

### With `--threshold` flags
- Example: `frai eval --outputs out.json --references ref.json --threshold exact_match=0.9 --threshold toxicity=1.0`
- Each threshold is checked against the corresponding metric score
- Exit codes:
  - **0**: All thresholds pass OR no thresholds specified
  - **1**: Any threshold fails (report written)
  - **2**: Usage error - malformed threshold or unknown metric (no report written)

### Edge Cases
- **Null Score**: Metrics with null scores (e.g., exact_match without references) automatically fail their threshold
- **Unknown Metric**: Error message lists all valid metric IDs
- **Out of Range**: Threshold values outside 0-1 rejected with clear error
- **Custom Metrics**: Works with custom metrics passed to `runEvaluations()`

## SDK Integration
SDK users can call `Eval.generateReport()` with thresholds:
```javascript
const report = Eval.generateReport({
  evaluations,
  outputsPath: 'outputs.json',
  referencesPath: 'refs.json',
  thresholds: { exact_match: 0.9, toxicity: 1.0 }
});
// report.passed = true/false
// report.thresholds = [{ metric, min, score, passed }, ...]
```

## Report Examples

### JSON Report
```json
{
  "metadata": { ... },
  "metrics": [ ... ],
  "passed": false,
  "thresholds": [
    { "metric": "exact_match", "min": 0.9, "score": 0.85, "passed": false },
    { "metric": "toxicity", "min": 1.0, "score": 1.0, "passed": true }
  ]
}
```

### Markdown Report
```markdown
## Thresholds

| Metric | Minimum | Score | Status |
|--------|---------|-------|--------|
| exact_match | 0.90 | 0.85 | ❌ FAIL |
| toxicity | 1.00 | 1.00 | ✅ PASS |
```

## Testing
All new functionality covered by tests in `frai-core/src/eval/index.test.js`:
- Threshold validation (valid/invalid inputs)
- Threshold evaluation (passing/failing scenarios)
- Null score handling
- Report generation with/without thresholds
- Markdown rendering with threshold table
